learning_outcomes.text: Knows the fundamental principles of mechanical systems operation and manufacturing technological processes.
Understands the methods of constructive-functional analysis and quality requirements applicable in the mechanical industry.
Knows occupational safety standards and specific fire safety instructions for working with mechanical equipment.
Understands the use of simulation software for calculating, dimensioning, and verifying mechanical components.
Is capable of performing diagnostic and maintenance operations on real mechanical equipment and systems.
Applies analysis and optimization methods for technological processes and mechanical components.
Uses measuring equipment and simulation programs to verify functional parameters.
Drafts technical reports and documentation related to practice activities, according to professional standards.
Demonstrates autonomy in performing practical tasks, respecting work procedures and safety standards.
Is capable of planning and individually managing diagnostic, technical maintenance, and reporting activities.
Demonstrates responsibility in the use of equipment and resources, ensuring the quality and safety of operations performed.
Integrates efficiently into multidisciplinary teams, respecting the ethical and collaborative principles of the profession.

syllabus_topics: Occupational safety, general instructions, specific instructions for the practice location, fire safety instructions
Preparation of the organizational sketch of the activity location
Description of technological processes in the sectors where the practice activity takes place
Constructive-functional analysis of technological lines, mechanical transmissions in the construction of road vehicles, thermal equipment, mechatronic equipment, and robots
Knowledge of main types of mechanical processing
General aspects regarding the use of calculation programs in the design of mechanical and mechatronic systems within the company or firm
teaching_methods: Applied demonstrations on mechanical equipment and systems
Case studies for analyzing technological processes and optimizing equipment function
Working with specific software for verifying functional parameters

assessment_methods.method: Practice report (oral presentation and direct communication with practice supervisor)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result at a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded. A minimum grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes and the granting of associated study credits. The practice report has a weight of 100% of the final grade and requires a minimum score of 5 for promotion.
